name: P N Gadgil Jewellers Ltd
title: P N Gadgil Jewellers Ltd - 544256 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Q2 FY27 revenue INR2,666 cr (+22%) and adjusted PAT margin 4.4% (from 3.3%), but store additions are back-loaded and the stock turn on new stores is ~1.1x, not yet proven at scale.

summary.headline: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR2,666 crore and EBITDA 57% to INR224.6 crore, with margin up 186 bps to 8.4%.
summary.overview: P N Gadgil reported Q2 FY27 revenue of about INR2,660-2,666 crore (up 22% YoY), EBITDA of INR224.6 crore (8.4% margin) and PAT of INR121.1 crore (4.5% margin), with profit growing roughly twice as fast as revenue. Retail grew 31% with SSSG of 25.5%, while e-commerce fell 84% after the company cut low-margin coin sales. Management said about INR200 crore of Navaratri sales shifted from Q2 into Q3 this year, and the company completed the Silvostyle acquisition on 1 October. Gross margin was down 50 bps QoQ, which management attributed to franchisee share rising to 17% from 12%.

financial_highlights.change: +32% YoY; margin +89 bps YoY, -50 bps QoQ

financial_highlights.metric: Adjusted EBITDA (excl. INR5 crore unhedged inventory gain)

financial_highlights.value: Revenue INR5,079 crore; PAT INR226.5 crore

segments.name: Retail
segments.commentary: Retail revenue INR2,061 crore, 77% of total (72% a year ago); stud ratio 11.9% vs 9% a year ago and 10.96% in Q1. Gold bars and coins fell to 15.8% of retail revenue from about 22%.

segments.name: Franchisee
segments.commentary: Franchisee revenue grew 35% YoY; franchisee share of revenue rose to 17% from 12%.

segments.name: E-commerce
segments.commentary: E-com revenue fell 84% YoY as low-margin coin sales were deliberately reduced in favour of jewellery.

segments.name: Diamond and gold jewellery
segments.commentary: Diamond jewellery value +21% and volume +11%; gold jewellery value +47% and volume +4%. Gold bar and coin value -24%, volume -48%.

segments.name: Northern and Central India
segments.commentary: Share of retail revenue from these regions rose to 2.7% from 0.7%; seven company-owned stores there show a stud ratio of 17.4%.

guidance_outlook: Open about 23 new stores in FY27 (8-10 in Q3, rest in Q4), taking the total to about 103 stores by year-end; 80 stores at quarter end (79 India, 1 US).
FY27 company revenue target of INR13,000 crore-plus; PAT margin guidance of 4.0-4.2%.
Three-year aspiration of about INR17,000 crore revenue by FY29 (25% CAGR FY27-29); another estimate of about INR21,000 crore by FY29 was given in the Q&A.
Stud ratio to rise to 17-18% at company level and newer geographies to reach 30-35% of sales by FY30 (Maharashtra currently about 91%).
Debt to fall 20-25% by FY29-FY30; the 170-odd store target by FY29 to be funded from internal accruals.
From FY28, store openings to split 50-50 between COCO and FOCO (franchise-owned); about 30-35 stores planned for the next year.
capex_capacity: Ayodhya store operational; Prayagraj store scheduled to open 4 November 2026.

UP stores (about 4 COCO stores in Lucknow, Kanpur, Gorakhpur, Banaras, plus Patna and Indore) averaging 11-12 months old, with stock turn about 1.1x and revenue run-rate about INR60 crore per store versus INR50-55 crore plan; target 8-10 UP stores by end FY27.
Mature-store targets for new regions: 2.5-3x stock turn, rising to 3.5-4x after year 4; revenue about INR200 crore per mature store; stud ratio 22-25%.
Inventory for new-region stores is about 10% of Maharashtra gold volume because they are stud-led.
Typical Maharashtra store carries gold inventory of about INR50-55 crore, roughly 30-32 kg.
Silvostyle acquired 100% on 1 October; it already runs 18 stores and about 68 shop-in-shops.
demand_pricing: Q2 is seasonally subdued (Chaturmas), but management said demand stayed healthy; customers shifted to lightweight, studded and old gold exchange.
Footfalls above 1.78 lakh, conversion 88.6%, average transaction value INR1.22 lakh.
Management said Navaratri was good, Diwali bookings are strong and prices are soft, which should lift volumes.
Gold-bar-to-jewellery conversion improved to 68% from 53% in Q1.
Made-to-order share is 22-25% in UP versus 30-32% in Maharashtra.
Management said without gold price increases mature-store SSSG is in the single digits (7-8%).

qa_highlights.question: Was there a festive shift affecting gross margin, and by how much?
qa_highlights.answer: Navaratri moved from Q2 last year into Q3 this year; about INR200 crore of revenue from the 10 days shifted. The 50 bps QoQ gross margin dip was attributed to franchisee mix rising to 17% from 12%.

qa_highlights.question: How will capital be allocated across franchise, COCO and new brands?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 is FOCO-led in Q3-Q4; from FY28 the split is 50-50 COCO/FOCO for both legacy and YOOU. Internal accruals are expected to fund COCO expansion, and debt is to fall 20-25% by 2030.

qa_highlights.question: How mature stores in UP are performing (turns, stud ratio, margin)?
qa_highlights.answer: Stock turn is about 1.1x (plan was 1x), revenue about INR60 crore per store (plan INR50-55 crore), stud ratio above 17% (plan 15%), gross margin about 35%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path for YOOU inventory turn and why did legacy turn fall to 3.7x?
qa_highlights.answer: YOOU is about 70% diamond and 30% gold, with a target of 1.8-2x turns at maturity against 0.8x now. Management said legacy turns of 3.7-4x are well above the 2-2.5x industry norm and are sustainable as new stores mature.

qa_highlights.question: How will the QIP proceeds and borrowing be deployed?
qa_highlights.answer: Part of the INR700 crore QIP went into festive working capital; the rest is in FDs (about INR1,191 crore, up INR637 crore QoQ). Gross borrowings rose about INR385 crore since March on GML loans, but net borrowings fell INR167 crore after collateral and FDs.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook for employee cost and other expenses in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Employee cost fell about INR6 crore QoQ on lower variable pay. Other expenses were INR86 crore in Q2 versus INR85 crore in Q1, and management expects similar moderation in H2.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure as franchisee mix rises (franchisee share 17% vs 12%) and as the FOCO model scales.
Store rollout concentration: 8-10 openings in Q3 and the balance in Q4, a steep back-loaded schedule.
Festive sales shift into Q3 makes Q2 vs Q3 comparisons noisy.
Gross borrowings and finance costs rising (about INR385 crore increase since March from GML loans); deleveraging targets depend on accruals.
YOOU inventory turn at 0.8x against a 1.8-2x target; the Silvostyle integration is new.
Dependence on stable gold prices; a gold price rise is expected to lower volumes.
Call quality was poor during the Q&A; some questions (for example Vikrant Kashyap's on non-Maharashtra contribution) went unanswered.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on growth, UP expansion, the store ramp and festive demand. More guarded on the specifics of the FY29 targets, which management called aspirational. Management also avoided some detail on the make-up of margins.
key_quotes: This reflects the strength of underlying operations and demonstrates that our margin expansion has been driven by operational improvements rather than gold price movements.
So what we're trying to say from all this is that our internal accruals should be more than enough to fund the COCO expansion, and we'll not be required to raise any further debt.
We had done a 3-year plan, which is more of an aspirational plan, but it will be difficult to right now pin a number to it.

adds.what: ~23 new stores in FY27 (8-10 in Q3, rest in Q4), taking total to ~103 by year-end; 80 at quarter end
Silvostyle acquired 100% on 1 Oct: 18 stores and ~68 shop-in-shops (acquired, not built)

growth.why: FY27 revenue target of INR13,000 crore-plus (about 13,000 crore vs. H1 revenue of 5,079 crore) backed by ~23 new stores in FY27 (8-10 in Q3, rest Q4) and Navaratri/Diwali demand commentary; no order book, so backing is partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin rose 186 bps YoY to 8.4% and stud ratio is 11.9% vs 9%, but gross margin fell 50 bps QoQ as franchisee share rose to 17% from 12%, and FY27 PAT margin guidance is 4.0-4.2% (Q2 at 4.5%).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About 23 new stores in FY27 (8-10 in Q3, rest in Q4) taking total to ~103 from 80 at quarter end; Prayagraj opens 4 Nov 2026 and Silvostyle's 18 stores are already acquired.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Retail revenue grew 31% with SSSG 25.5%, Diwali bookings are strong and prices are soft, but management said SSSG without gold price increases is only 7-8%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Utilisation and capex were not disclosed, but store rollout is funded from internal accruals and FY28 plan of 30-35 stores is set, so a further capex disclosure is possible rather than a firm announcement.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q2 revenue grew 22% and PAT 53%, Diwali bookings are strong and UP stores run at about INR60 crore per store versus a INR50-55 crore plan, but about INR200 crore of Navaratri sales shifted into Q3 and the gain is partly timing.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Store rollout is steeply back-loaded (8-10 in Q3, rest in Q4), gross borrowings rose about INR385 crore since March, and the FY27 INR13,000 crore-plus target needs H2 revenue of about INR8,000 crore against H1's INR5,079 crore.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: From FY28 store openings split 50-50 between COCO and FOCO for both legacy and YOOU, and YOOU is only about 0.8x turn against a 1.8-2x target, so new-format rollout is planned but not dated.

rows.label: Northern and Central India expansion
rows.why: Share of retail revenue from these regions rose to 2.7% from 0.7%, and seven stores there show a 17.4% stud ratio; the UP stores run at about INR60 crore per store, and the target is 8-10 UP stores by end FY27.

rows.label: Debt down 20-25% by FY29-FY30
rows.why: Management targets a 20-25% borrowing cut funded from accruals, but gross borrowings rose about INR385 crore since March and the 170-store target by FY29 competes for the same cash.

rows.label: Hedge coverage raised to about 80%
rows.why: Management is raising hedge cover to about 80% to make earnings more resilient to gold price swings, a direct action already in place.

tone.note: Management was confident on store ramp, UP expansion, festive demand and FY27 revenue of INR13,000 crore-plus, but called the FY29 targets aspirational and was thin on margin make-up; analysts pushed on gross margin and unanswered questions on non-Maharashtra contribution.
